headline: High: LightAgent’s broad network/MCP/tooling can amplify unsafe interactions, while godot_rl_agents appears non-runnable and low-risk on its own.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and parses tool-call workflows, so attacker-controlled content could steer it if fed through shared channels. godot_rl_agents has no documented I/O surfaces, so the pairwise bridge is one-sided and indirect. The pathway is plausible in default agent workflows, but not directly evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF LightAgent ingests content from a shared file, MCP server, or clipboard without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF godot_rl_agents is used as a content source for LightAgent, injected instructions can propagate through that bridge.
mitigations: Disable untrusted MCP sources for LightAgent.
Add provenance tags to any content passed from godot_rl_agents to LightAgent.
Require a human review step before LightAgent acts on external text.
Use allowlisted prompts/templates only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, and it has broad network egress. godot_rl_agents is open-source with no documented data-touching surfaces, so leakage risk is mainly from LightAgent exporting paired workflow data if the two are connected. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF LightAgent receives any outputs, logs, or artifacts derived from godot_rl_agents, those data classes can be transmitted off-host.
IF LightAgent is configured with external APIs, its broad egress can leak paired workflow state or secrets.
mitigations: Remove secrets from LightAgent inputs.
Restrict LightAgent network egress to approved endpoints.
Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Turn off long-term memory for sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no write, network, or concurrency surfaces, while LightAgent supports subprocesses, MCP, and multiple instances. There is no documented shared mutable resource between them, so direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because LightAgent’s runtime can mutate workflow state if connected to shared resources.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or MCP-backed resource, write conflicts can occur.
IF LightAgent runs multiple instances against shared state, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Disable concurrent LightAgent instances on shared state.
Add file locks around any shared artifacts.
Keep godot_rl_agents read-only.
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can act on tool results and workflow state, so if it consumes outputs from godot_rl_agents without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. godot_rl_agents is a simulation/RL project with no documented validation layer for its outputs. The pairwise pathway exists, but the blast radius is limited to workflow correctness rather than irreversible harm.
conditions: IF LightAgent treats outputs from godot_rl_agents as authoritative, unverified errors can propagate.
IF LightAgent uses those outputs to drive tool calls or state changes, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before LightAgent acts on external outputs.
Insert a human approval step for consequential actions.
Log source provenance on every handoff.
Use schema validation on exchanged messages.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, and secrets, while godot_rl_agents is open-source and non-runnable with no documented data residency controls. If paired in a workflow that moves regulated data into LightAgent, retention and residency obligations may diverge. Only LightAgent is cited because the compliance surface is on its side; godot_rl_agents has no relevant residency or retention fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed into LightAgent, its memory and trace retention must satisfy the applicable policy.
IF the deployment requires residency or deletion guarantees, LightAgent must be configured to meet them before use.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to LightAgent.
Disable or shorten retention for memory and traces.
Review vendor DPA and residency terms.
Purge stored conversations before pairing.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
